lessons.title: Who is the cutoff?
script: When the ball goes to the outfield, one infielder goes out to be the cutoff. The outfielder throws to that player, not all the way to the base.
On a single, the cutoff is the lead player for the throw to second base.
Single to left field: the shortstop goes out. The second baseman covers second base.
Single to right field: the second baseman goes out. The shortstop covers second base.
Single to center field: the middle infielder on the side the ball is hit goes out. On a ball right up the middle, most teams send the shortstop.
On a double in the gap or down the line, two infielders go out. This is called a double cut.
Ball to the left-center gap or down the left-field line: the shortstop is the lead. The second baseman is the trail.
Ball to the right-center gap or down the right-field line: the second baseman is the lead. The shortstop is the trail.
The trail stands 15 to 20 feet behind the lead, on the same line. If the throw is short, high or gets past the lead, the trail catches it.
Every team sets its own plan for some plays, so learn your coach's plan too.

lessons.title: Where the cutoff lines up
script: Stand on a straight line from the outfielder to the base the ball is going to.
Go out far enough that the outfielder can reach you on the fly with a strong throw.
Open your chest to the outfielder so you can see the ball and the field.
Get both hands up high, above your head, so the outfielder has a big target.
Yell for the ball so the outfielder can find you fast. Most teams yell "Hit me! Hit me!"
Catch the ball on your glove side. Then turn to your glove side and throw to the base.
If the player at the base tells you to move left or right, move quickly and get your hands back up.

lessons.title: Listen for the call
script: The player at the target base makes the call. On a throw home, that is the catcher. On a throw to third, that is the third baseman.
They make the call because they can see the runner and the ball at the same time. The cutoff cannot.
"Cut!" means catch the ball and hold it.
"Cut two!" means catch the ball and throw it to second base. The number tells you which base to throw to.
"Relay!" means catch the ball and throw it on to the target base. You hear this when the throw is off line or will not make it all the way.
No call means let the ball go through to the base. Do not touch it.
Call loud and call early. Say it more than once so the cutoff hears it over the crowd.

checks.prompt: A ball rolls to the right-center gap for a double. The second baseman goes out as the lead. What does the shortstop do?
choices: Trails 15 to 20 feet behind the second baseman, on the same line
Runs out next to the outfielder

feedback.correct: Yes. The shortstop is the trail. The trail backs up the lead in case the throw is short or gets past.
feedback.wrong: Not quite. On a ball to the right side, the second baseman is the lead and the shortstop trails 15 to 20 feet behind.

choices: On a straight line from the outfielder to the target base
Behind the pitcher's mound every time

feedback.correct: Right. On the straight line, a good throw is easy to catch or let go through.
feedback.wrong: Try again. The cutoff stands on a straight line from the outfielder to the base the ball is going to.

checks.prompt: You are the cutoff. The catcher yells "Cut two!" What do you do?
choices: Catch the ball and hold it
Catch the ball and throw it home
Catch the ball and throw it to second base

feedback.correct: Yes. "Cut two" means catch it and throw to second base.
feedback.wrong: Not quite. The number tells you the base. "Cut two" means catch it and throw to second base.

drills.title: Relay race lines
drills.setup: Make two or more lines of four or five players. Space players in each line about 60 feet apart. The first player in each line has a ball.
steps: On "Go", the first player throws to the next player in the line.
Each player opens up, gets hands up and yells for the ball.
Catch on your glove side, turn to your glove side and throw to the next player.
When the ball reaches the end, send it back down the line.
The first line to get the ball back to the start wins.
drills.reps: 3 races. Change the order of each line after every race.
coachingPoints: Hands up and loud before the ball is thrown.
Turn to the glove side. Do not spin the long way.
A good, chest-high throw beats a fast, wild throw.
If the ball is dropped, the player who dropped it chases it and goes on from there.

drills.title: Cutoff alignment with a coach call
drills.setup: Put outfielders in left, center and right. Put a cutoff player in the infield and a catcher or coach at home plate. A coach hits or rolls balls to the outfield.
steps: The coach sends a ball to one outfielder.
The cutoff runs to the line between that outfielder and home plate and gets hands up.
The catcher calls "Cut", "Cut two", "Relay" or nothing at all.
The cutoff does what the call says: hold it, throw to second, throw it home, or let it go through.
Rotate the outfielders and cutoff players every few balls.
coachingPoints: Get on the line first, then get your hands up.
The catcher calls early and loud, more than once.
Move left or right when the catcher says so.
No call means do not touch the ball.

drills.title: Double cut on a ball in the gap
drills.setup: Put players at shortstop, second base, third base and catcher, with two outfielders in the gaps. A coach hits or rolls balls into the left-center and right-center gaps.
steps: The coach sends a ball into one gap.
On a ball to the left side, the shortstop goes out as the lead and the second baseman trails. On a ball to the right side, they switch.
The trail lines up 15 to 20 feet behind the lead, on the same line.
The outfielder throws to the lead. The lead catches, turns and throws to third base or home.
If the throw is short or gets past the lead, the trail catches it and makes the throw.
coachingPoints: The trail is not a spectator. Be ready for every throw.
The trail stays on the same line as the lead.
The lead goes out far enough to make the outfielder's throw short and strong.
The player at the target base makes the call.

drills.title: Trail backup on a double down the line
drills.setup: Put a lead and a trail out near the foul line in left field, and a third baseman at third. A coach stands in the outfield corner with a bucket of balls.
steps: The lead lines up between the coach and third base. The trail lines up 15 to 20 feet behind the lead.
The coach throws to the lead. Some throws are good. Some are short, high or wide on purpose.
On a good throw, the lead catches it, turns and throws to third.
On a bad throw, the trail catches it and throws to third.
Do the same drill down the right-field line with the second baseman as the lead.
drills.reps: 8 throws per pair down each line, then switch lead and trail.
coachingPoints: The trail watches the ball, not the lead.
The trail can call out the base so the lead knows where to throw.
Stay in a ready stance. A bad throw comes fast.
Knock down a ball in the dirt. Keep it in front of you.

drills.title: Hit-the-cutoff target throws
drills.setup: Pair each outfielder with a partner who plays the cutoff, about 90 to 120 feet apart. The cutoff stands with hands up high.
steps: The cutoff gets hands up and yells for the ball.
The outfielder takes a crow hop and throws at the cutoff's head.
Score 2 points for a throw that reaches the cutoff on the fly between the shoulders and the top of the hands.
Score 1 point for a throw the cutoff can catch without moving their feet.
Switch jobs after each round.
coachingPoints: Find the cutoff before you throw. Look for the hands.
Aim at the head. A throw that sails a little high is easier to handle than one in the dirt.
Throw over the top so the ball goes straight.
A low, strong throw to the cutoff beats a high, looping throw to the base.

drills.title: Field it and hit the cutoff
drills.setup: Put outfielders in a line in center field. Put a cutoff player between them and second base. A coach rolls or hits ground balls to the outfielders.
steps: The coach sends a ground ball to the first outfielder.
The outfielder charges the ball and fields it on the glove side.
The outfielder finds the cutoff, takes a crow hop and throws at the cutoff's head.
The cutoff catches it, turns to the glove side and throws to second base.
The outfielder goes to the back of the line.
drills.reps: 2 rounds of 5 balls for each outfielder.
coachingPoints: Charge the ball. Every step you take saves time.
Get your feet moving toward the cutoff before you throw.
Look for the cutoff's hands, then throw.
Keep the throw low and on line so the cutoff can catch it or let it go.
